svg.aria-label: What is inside BOOT.BIN: a 2,240-byte Zynq boot header (width detection word, XNLX identifier, image offset 0x8C0, image size, load address 0, checksum) followed by the U-Boot SPL; and what the SPL's first call, ps7_init, does: set the MIO pin muxes, start the PLLs, set the clock dividers, initialise the DDR3L controller and enable the peripherals; the programmable logic is not configured.
svg.text: Inside BOOT.BIN, and what the SPL's first call (ps7_init) does
BOOT.BIN is 131,676 bytes in this build: a 2,240-byte Zynq boot header and the SPL. Its first job is to make the DDR3L usable.
width detection: the BootROM checks the bus width
image offset: where the payload starts
image size in bytes (131,676, the whole file)
image load: the SPL runs at address 0 (OCM)
register-init list: unused, ps7_init does the work
129,436 bytes of ARM code and data plus U-Boot's SPL device tree:
ps7_init_gpl.o (the register writes), the UART and SD drivers,
a FAT reader, a FIT parser; linked to run at address 0.
The BootROM copies it into OCM, so it must stay under 192 KiB.
No FSBL, no bitstream, no U-Boot proper in this file. Those are:
u-boot.img: a separate FAT file the SPL loads by name,
the PL bitstream: not used for the first boot (docs/13).
ps7_init(), THE FIRST THING THE SPL DOES (board_init_f in arch/arm/mach-zynq/spl.c)
mux the 54 MIO pins: UART0 on 14/15, SD0 on 40-45, Ethernet
RGMII on 16-27, USB on 28-39, QSPI on 1-6
start ARM, DDR and IO PLLs from the 33.3333 MHz PS_CLK and wait
dividers for the CPUs, the DDR, the UART, SD and Ethernet; the
program the DDR controller for DDR3, 32-bit data bus, 1 GiB;
poll the DCI calibration and the controller until DDR is up
UART and QSPI controller registers, SMC timing, DDR termination,
the PL power-on-reset registers; then lock the SLCR again
Why this is a table of register writes
Each array is a list of EMIT_WRITE / EMIT_MASKWRITE / EMIT_MASKPOLL records:
an address, a mask and a value. ps7_config() walks the list and does them.
The file holds three copies (silicon 1.0, 2.0, 3.0); ps7_init() reads the chip's
revision and picks one. Vivado generates all of it from the board preset.
The SPL initialises its console (you see "U-Boot SPL 2026.07…"), sets up the SD host, opens u-boot.img on the FAT partition and jumps to it in DDR.
ps7_init does NOT configure the programmable logic. The PL needs a bitstream, which this build does not load.
Header layout: tools/zynqimage.c; values read from this build's spl/boot.bin with mkimage -l and a hex dump. The 192 KiB limit is CONFIG_SPL_MAX_SIZE=0x30000.
ps7_init_gpl.c: generated by Vivado 2019.1 for Digilent's Eclypse Z7 preset; this file is downloaded, not committed (docs/03-uboot-spl.md). Pins: UG585 and the Eclypse Z7 reference manual.
